newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen dip in dull trade, downside limited.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen dip in dull trade, downside limited.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures backed off slightly in a listless session on Wednesday, but dealers said the market looked well supported on the lower end and was likely to consolidate in a new range after last week's tankan report.
Interest was limited by a dearth of fresh news and economic data, dealers said.
A trader with an Asian futures house said the yen's firmer tone against the dollar in early trade gave some support to the short-term Japanese interest rate futures.
He said June Euroyen looked set to trade between 99.32/33 and 99.37/38 in the near term.
It was quoted unchanged against its IMM close at 99.35 at 1115 GMT. September was at 99.22 against 99.24. Turnover for both months was low at 4,010 and 4,000 contracts respectively.
The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract settled at 126.20 against its previous 126.15.
Dealers said the contract rose initially on expectations of a slide in the Nikkei but subsided when this failed to materialise.
Support is seen at 125.80 and resistance at 126.45/50.
Eurodollar futures scarcely flinched all day and the March contract ended unchanged against its IMM close at 94.54 on meagre turnover of 1,545 lots.
Dealers said interest was hampered by anticipation of U.S. payrolls data for November, due on Friday, and the traditional slowdown in activity ahead of the year end.
Market expectations call for a 170,000 rise in non-farm payrolls and a 5.2 percent unemployment rate.
"Eurodollars look pretty overbought. The topside should be capped at 94.57/58 on the Marches and 94.50 on the Junes," said the trader.
